ORPP team reflects on AI use and implication to regulatory role 

The @ORPPKenya  leadership,management  and section of staff in a two-day AI training, 24th and 25th Sept,2026 to place and explore  appropriate employment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in @ORPPKenya  processes.
 
In the the forum,the participants  explored challenges ,opportunities and realities of AI in a rapidly changing tech. ecosystem .

The Registrar J.C. Lorionokou, noted AI is increasingly becoming part of the way institutions work and process information.

“The @ORPPKenya should keep pace to such technical advancements.We will endeavour to embrace such in ORPP processing of information and other roles we undertake ,” the Registrar said.
Further, he noted that AI is no longer simply a subject for technology experts, but a tool that is increasingly influencing everyday work, communication and decision-making.

Assistant Registrar CPA,CS Agatha Wahome urged for the need to responsibly  embrace  technology ,emphasizing that all professionals must enhance their knowledge as AI is no longer a preserve ICT experts.

"A well-functioning political party system requires ,beyond the traditional regulatory mechanims, adoption of  necessary tools and technologies that enhance monitoring ” said HSF (check) Uta Statschewski who supported the training in collaboration with Centre for Intellectual Property and Information Technology Law, Strathmore University.

The training aligns Data Transformation and Data Management,one of the @ORPPKenya    current strategic focus in the Strategic Plan aiming at harnessing Tech and data management in 2025-2028 strategic period  future demands of public service.

Highlights Of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s National Statement Delivered By Vice President @KashimSM Shettima At General Debate Of 81st UNGA

1. President Tinubu reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to multilateralism, insisting that diplomacy, cooperation and international law must prevail over coercion, isolation and the arbitrary use of power.

2. President Tinubu called for urgent reform of the United Nations Security Council, declaring that the world of 2026 cannot remain governed by the power structure of 1945.

3. Nigeria demanded at least two permanent seats for Africa, with full rights and responsibilities, including the veto for as long as it exists, as well as five non-permanent seats in line with the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration.

4. The President expressed Nigeria's readiness to assume greater global responsibility, drawing on decades of peacekeeping, mediation and security interventions across Africa, including Liberia, Sierra Leone, Darfur, Mali and The Gambia.

5. President Tinubu linked Nigeria’s foreign policy to its domestic economic reforms, stressing that sound macroeconomic management, stronger institutions, strategic investment and private-sector development are central to sustainable growth.

6. Nigeria rejected the false choice between development and climate action, insisting that developing countries must be allowed to industrialise, reduce poverty and expand energy access while pursuing lower-carbon growth.

7. President Tinubu called for predictable climate finance, technology transfer and capacity building, stressing that climate responsibility must be based on equity and shared responsibility rather than charity.

8. Nigeria reaffirmed its Energy Transition Plan and net-zero target for 2060, combining renewable energy, clean cooking, gas as a transition fuel, climate-smart agriculture and nature-based solutions.

9. President Tinubu urged the world not to surrender the future of Artificial Intelligence to fear, saying AI should be harnessed to transform healthcare, education, agriculture, governance and economic productivity.

10. Nigeria invited global partners to work with its youthful population in technology and innovation, while expanding investments in digital public infrastructure, broadband, research and technology entrepreneurship.

11. President Tinubu called for a radical reform of the international financial architecture, wider access to concessional financing and debt frameworks that allow developing countries to invest in education, healthcare and infrastructure.

12. Nigeria identified the African Continental Free Trade Area as a major engine of Africa’s transformation, urging the continent to move from raw-material exports to value addition, manufacturing, innovation and knowledge-driven growth.

13. On security, Nigeria called for stronger intelligence sharing, tighter controls on terrorist financing and illicit arms flows, stressing that military victories must be reinforced by education, opportunity, accountable governance and social inclusion.

14. President Tinubu called for urgent diplomacy in Sudan and other conflict zones, insisting that civilians must be protected, humanitarian access guaranteed and international law respected.

15. Nigeria pledged to choose cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over division and partnership over isolation, declaring that a reformed, inclusive and effective United Nations remains indispensable to global peace, justice and sustainable development.

#UNGA81 #NigeriaAtUNGA

@MTWAUganda convened a broad stakeholder engagement to examine how digital technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can reshape Uganda’s tourism sector and position the destination more effectively in the digital traveller’s journey.

The engagement brought together key players across the tourism and technology ecosystem, including the private sector, line MDAs, @UTAUganda, @PSF_UGANDA innovators, technology stakeholders, academia and students, whose perspectives are critical to shaping the future of tourism.

Discussions explored how AI can strengthen destination marketing, improve visitor experiences, enhance access to tourism information, support data-driven decision-making, create new business opportunities and increase the visibility of Uganda’s diverse tourism products.

Participants were also encouraged to move beyond discussion and contribute practical ideas. Submissions werr submitted from the different sectors represented, highlighting opportunities, challenges, innovations and actionable interventions that can advance Uganda’s digital tourism agenda.

Google is sending an AI data center into space — with help from Elon Musk’s SpaceX

Google plans to launch a prototype satellite with four artificial intelligence chips aboard a SpaceXFalcon 9 rocket on October 1, 2026. [1, 2]
This mission is part of an experimental initiative called Project Suncatcher. It tests whether computer infrastructure for AI can move into space to save energy on Earth. [1, 2, 3]

Mission Details
•Launch Date: October 1, 2026
•
•Location: Vandenberg Space Force Base near Santa Barbara, California
•
•Rocket: SpaceX Falcon 9 (on the Transporter-18 mission)
•
•The Satellite: A fridge-sized prototype named MVP built with [Planet Labs]. It carries the power of a single ground server. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
•

What is Project Suncatcher?
•The Goal: Google wants to see if space is a safe place for artificial intelligence. [1]
•
•The Hardware: The satellite carries four TPUs (Tensor Processing Units). These are specialized computer chips that Google uses to run AI and machine learning. [1, 2]
•
•The Tests: The mission checks if the chips can survive the violent shaking of a rocket launch. It also tests how the chips handle intense space radiation and extreme heat or cold.[1, 2, 3]
•

Why Put Computers in Space?
•More Power: Satellites get near-constant sunlight. They can generate up to eight times more solar power than solar panels placed on Earth.
•
•Grid Relief: Earth's electrical grids are struggling to keep up with the massive power demands of ground-based AI data centers.
•
•Cooling: Space is a vacuum, which changes how heat behaves compared to Earth. [1, 2, 3]
•

Future Plans
•Google is not putting a full data center into orbit yet. This first launch is a small test.
•
•If the test works, Google plans to launch two more satellites in 2027.
•
•The long-term vision is to connect many small satellites into a network that works together as an orbiting data center. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
•

Would you like to know more about how companies cool computers in space or the energy challenges facing AI on Earth?
